items.title: Section: Gentleness — The Six Points of Harmony

items.zh: 云何柔和？謂如有一，於大師等具足成就慈愍身業，具足成就慈愍語業，具足成就慈愍意業。與諸有智同梵行者和同受用應所受用；凡所飲食無有私密，如法所獲、如法所得，墮在鉢中，為鉢所攝而為受用。同戒、同見，成就如是六種可樂、可愛、可重，無違諍法，易可共住，性不惱他。與諸有智同梵行者共住一處，常令歡喜。是名柔和。
items.en: What is gentleness? It is like one who is fully accomplished in loving bodily conduct, loving verbal conduct, and loving mental conduct towards the Teacher and others; who shares alike with wise fellow practitioners in what should be shared, keeping nothing of one's food hidden or private, and using what is rightfully gained and rightfully received as what has fallen into the bowl and is held by the bowl [in common]; and who shares equally in precepts and in view. Accomplished in these six qualities — lovable, admirable, and respected, free of contention, easy to live alongside, never causing others distress — one who dwells together with wise fellow practitioners constantly brings them joy. This is called gentleness.

items.title: Section: Innate Goodness Completes All Seventeen Ornaments

items.zh: 云何賢善？謂如有一，遠離顰蹙，舒顏平視，含笑先言，常為愛語，性多攝受善法同侶，身心澄淨。是名賢善。
items.en: What is innate goodness? It is like one who is free of a furrowed brow, whose face is open and gaze level, who smiles and speaks first, whose words are always kind, who naturally draws good companions in the Dharma, and whose body and mind are genuinely clear and pure. This is called innate goodness.

items.title: Section: A Second List Opens — Sixteen Things to Abstain From

items.zh: 若有成就如是諸法，愛樂正法、愛樂功德；
items.en: If one has accomplished these qualities, one delights in the true teaching and delights in genuine virtue —

items.title: Section: Eight Disciplines of Genuine Restraint

items.zh: 不樂利養恭敬稱譽。亦不成就增益、損減二種邪見。於非有法未甞增益，於實有法未甞損減。於諸世間事文綺者，所造順世種種字相綺飾文句相應詩論，能正了知無義無利，遠避、棄捨、不習、不愛，亦不流傳。不樂貯畜餘長衣鉢。遠離在家共諠雜住，增煩惱故。樂與聖眾和合居止，淨修智故。不樂攝受親里朋友。勿我由此親友因緣，當招無量擾亂事務；彼或變壞，當生種種愁慼、傷歎、悲苦、憂惱。隨所生起本隨二惑，不堅執著，尋即棄捨、除遣、變吐。
items.en: One does not delight in gain, honour, or praise. Nor does one hold either of the two distorted views, exaggeration or denial. … Regarding worldly ornamental writing … one correctly recognises it as meaningless and unprofitable, and avoids, abandons, never practices, never enjoys, and never circulates it. One does not delight in hoarding robes or bowls beyond what is needed. One avoids dwelling amid the noisy company of householders, since it increases affliction; one delights instead in dwelling together with the noble assembly, since it purifies wisdom. One does not delight in taking on relatives and friends as attachments, lest their affairs bring endless disturbance, or their misfortune bring grief, lamentation, sorrow, and distress. Whatever root or secondary afflictions arise, one does not cling to them firmly, but at once abandons, dispels, and expels them.

items.zh: 勿我由此二惑因緣，當生現法後法眾苦。

items.title: Section: Integrity Towards Donors, Towards Oneself, and Towards the Training

items.zh: 終不虛損所有信施，終不毀犯清淨禁戒受用信施，終不毀呰他人信施。終不棄捨所受學處。常樂省察己之過失，不喜伺求他所愆犯。隱覆自善，發露己惡。命難因緣，亦不故思毀犯眾罪；設由忘念，少有所犯，即便速疾如法悔除。於應作事翹勤無墮，凡百所為自能成辦，終不求他為己給使。
items.en: One never squanders the faith-offerings received, never violates pure discipline while receiving them, and never disparages the offerings received by others. One never abandons the training undertaken. One habitually delights in examining one's own faults, taking no pleasure in searching out others' transgressions. One conceals one's own good qualities and openly discloses one's own faults. Even at the risk of one's life, one never deliberately commits an offence; and should a fault arise through forgetfulness, one swiftly confesses and corrects it as the training prescribes. Diligent in whatever should be done, one accomplishes ordinary tasks oneself, never requiring another to serve at one's command.

items.title: Section: The Final Two Disciplines Close All Thirty-Three Qualities

items.zh: 於佛世尊及佛弟子不可思議威德神力、甚深法教深生信解，終不毀謗；能正了知唯是如來所知所見，非我境界。終不樂住自妄見取、非理僻執、惡見所生言論呪術。
items.en: Towards the Buddha and his disciples' inconceivable majestic power and profound teaching, one gives rise to deep faith and understanding, never slandering them, correctly recognising that such things belong only to what the Tathāgata himself knows and sees, not to one's own present understanding. One never delights in dwelling in one's own false views, unreasonable and distorted grasping, or the doctrines and incantations born of wrong view.

items.title: Section: The True Meaning of Adornment

items.zh: 若與如是功德相應，如是安住、如是修學，以正沙門諸莊嚴具而自莊嚴，甚為微妙。譬如有人，盛壯端正，好自莊嚴，樂受諸欲，沐浴身首，塗以妙香，服鮮白衣，飾以種種妙莊嚴具。所謂瓔珞、耳環、指環、腕釧、臂釧、諸妙寶印，并金銀等種種華鬘。如是莊嚴極為奇妙。如是行者，以正沙門種種功德妙莊嚴具而自莊嚴，其德熾然，威光遍照，是故說為沙門莊嚴。是名沙門莊嚴具義。
items.en: One who is possessed of these qualities, abiding and training in this way, adorns oneself with the true ornaments of a renunciant — an adornment of the most subtle and excellent kind. It is like a person in the full vigour of youth, handsome and fine, who loves to adorn the body and delights in sensual pleasure: bathing head and body, anointing it with fine perfume, dressing in bright, clean garments, and adorning it with every manner of fine ornament — necklaces, earrings, rings, bracelets, armlets, fine jewelled seals, gold and silver, and garlands of every kind — adornment of the most exquisite sort. Just so, such a practitioner, adorned with the true and excellent ornaments of a renunciant's many virtues, blazes forth in splendour, majestic light shining everywhere. This is therefore called the ornaments of a renunciant — this is the meaning of a renunciant's ornaments.

blocks.text: The last ornaments and a closing image. With this, all fourteen provisions of the Stage of Departure are complete.

"Loving bodily, verbal, and mental conduct towards the Teacher and others; sharing alike with fellow practitioners in what should be shared": the six points of harmony. Even rightfully obtained food is not kept hidden; "what falls into the bowl is held by the bowl and shared".
"Free of a furrowed brow, face open and gaze level, smiling and speaking first, words always kind." It is a description of a person one would want to be near.
Such a person delights in the true teaching; does not delight in gain or praise; holds neither exaggerating nor denying views; avoids meaningless worldly writing.

"One never squanders the faith-offerings received." "One conceals one's own good qualities and openly discloses one's own faults." Master Cháng Bǎi: towards others, the opposite: conceal their faults and praise their virtues.
Towards the Buddha's inconceivable power and profound teaching, one has deep faith "and never slanders them, recognising that such things are known only to the Tathāgata".
"Like a person in the full vigour of youth, handsome and adorned": such a practitioner, "adorned with the true ornaments of a renunciant's many virtues, blazes forth in splendour."
The fourteen provisions are now complete. They are the groundwork. Fascicle 26 turns to the Stage of Departure's next topic: the kinds of persons who practise, and the objects of meditation.

quiz.q: Among the six points of harmony, what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "falling into the bowl, held by the bowl, and used" means?
options: sharing gains equally — what is rightly received goes into the bowl for common use
quiz.why: The text: keeping nothing of rightfully obtained food hidden — what falls into the bowl is held by the bowl and used. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is sharing gains equally. The English omits "falling into the bowl."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi sum up "concealing one's good and disclosing one's faults"?
options: for others, hide their faults and praise their good; for oneself, hide one's good and show one's faults
quiz.why: "One conceals one's own good qualities and openly discloses one's own faults." Master Cháng Bǎi: towards others, conceal their faults and praise their good; towards oneself, conceal one's good and reveal one's faults.

quiz.q: The text compares worldly adornment with jewellery. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say a renunciant's adornment is not?
options: not shaving the head and beard and putting on fine robes
quiz.why: "Such a practitioner, adorned with the true and excellent ornaments of a renunciant's many virtues, blazes forth in splendour." Venerable Miào Jìng: adornment does not mean shaving the head and beard and wearing good robes; it is the thirty-three virtues — seventeen plus sixteen.
